title: Week 9 BST Drill
footer: Written from the Week 9 lecture and lab (BST part only). New tree, not the practice quiz. Walks, paths and heights were checked in Python (revision/tools/w9_bst.py).

sections.label: Section 1
sections.name: Walks, search, successor
sections.figcap: Use this BST for every question in sections 1 and 2.

qs.p: What is the inorder walk of this tree?
qs.ex: Inorder is left, root, right, which for a BST is simply the keys sorted from smallest to largest. Option A goes level by level, C is postorder and D is preorder.

qs.p: What is the preorder walk of this tree?
qs.ex: Preorder writes each node before its children: 41, then the whole left part (20, 11, 29, 26, 32), then the whole right part (65, 50, 91, 72, 99). Option B goes level by level, which is a different walk.

qs.p: What is the postorder walk of this tree?
qs.ex: Postorder writes each node after both its children. Left part: 11, then 26, 32, 29, then 20. Right part: 50, then 72, 99, 91, then 65. Root 41 last. The root is always the last key in postorder.

qs.p: Searching for 32, which nodes are compared, in order?
qs.ex: 32 < 41, go left to 20. 32 > 20, go right to 29. 32 > 29, go right to 32. Found. Option C lists the sorted keys up to 32, which is not how search works.

qs.p: What is the successor of 32 (the next bigger key)?
qs.ex: 32 has no right child, so climb: 32 is the right child of 29, keep going. 29 is the right child of 20, keep going. 20 is the LEFT child of 41, so stop: 41. Check: in the sorted list, 41 comes right after 32.
41 has a right child 65. Go right to 65, then left as far as possible: 50. Check: in the sorted list, 50 comes right after 41.

sections.label: Section 2
sections.name: Insert, delete, height and running time

qs.p: Where does 30 go when it is inserted into this tree?
qs.ex: 30 < 41 go left to 20. 30 > 20 go right to 29. 30 > 29 go right to 32. 30 < 32 go left: empty. So 30 becomes the left child of 32. A new key always becomes a leaf.

qs.p: 65 has two children. When 65 is deleted, which key takes its place?
qs.ex: Two children: use the successor. Go right once (91), then left as far as possible (72). 72 moves into 65's place and 91's left child becomes empty. 50 is the predecessor, which the lecture does not use.

qs.p: What is the height of this tree?
qs.ex: Height counts EDGES on the longest path from the root to a leaf. 41, 20, 29, 26 has 3 edges (it has 4 nodes, which is the trap in option A).

qs.p: The keys 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 are inserted into an empty BST in that order. What is the height, and what is the worst-case search time for a BST with n keys?
qs.ex: Each key is bigger than all before it, so each goes to the right: a single chain 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 with 4 edges. Search on a chain checks every node, so the worst case is O(n). It is O(log n) only when the tree is balanced.

qs.p: What is the running time of an inorder walk of a BST with n nodes?
qs.ex: A walk visits every node exactly once whatever the shape, so it is Θ(n). The single-path operations (search, insert, successor and so on) are the ones that are O(h).
